source_batch.unit_label: Module C unit 5 (courseware unit 21): credit delivery and straight through processing

facts.statement: Before parting with money the bank must settle which documents to obtain from the borrower and guarantor so that it has legal recourse on default, whether a charge is to be created on the primary or collateral security and how, whether the charge must be registered with a prescribed authority, whether the securities are to be in the possession of the borrower or the bank, how the loan is to be disbursed, and what RBI guidelines say. Documents are signed by the borrower and guarantors so that the bank can establish liability in court; the borrower also signs documents creating charge over the primary security; the owner of collateral security who is not the borrower must first become a guarantor of the loan and then create the charge. Points for the credit officer: documents are properly stamped (stamp duty varies from State to State); the date of execution is never earlier than the date of stamping, and date and place of execution are stated; the parties have authority and capacity to contract (for example a partner signs on behalf of the firm, not in an individual capacity); the person signing does so of free will; documents are filled in before they are signed.

In the courseware's account, in the case of companies the charge should be registered with the Registrar of Companies within 30 days from the date of execution of the documents; documents requiring registration with the sub-registrar are registered within the prescribed time limit; all security interests and mortgage charges (except charges on vehicles shown in the Vahan site) are registered in the Central Registry of Securitisation Asset Reconstruction and Security Interest of India (CERSAI), because under the SARFAESI Act secured creditors enforce securities only if the security interest is filed with CERSAI; charge on certain assets is additionally registered with specific authorities (aircraft with the Director General of Civil Aviation, ships with the Mercantile Marine Department).
facts.locator: S01 printed p. 484 (not checked against the Companies Act or SARFAESI Act text)

facts.statement: CERSAI is a Government company licensed under section 8 of the Companies Act, 2013 that operates the Central Registry under the SARFAESI Act, 2002; the records are open to search by any lender or person dealing with the property, which prevents frauds involving multiple lending against the same property and sale of a property without disclosing the security interest; under section 23 of the SARFAESI Act every transaction of security interest is required to be filed with the Registry. A Government of India Gazette notification of 22 January 2016 provides for filing on the CERSAI portal the creation, modification or satisfaction of security interest in: immovable property by mortgage other than mortgage by deposit of title deeds; hypothecation of plant and machinery, stocks, debts including book debts or receivables, existing or future; intangible assets such as know-how, patent, copyright, trademark, licence and franchise; and under-construction residential or commercial property by an agreement or instrument other than mortgage. A bank files the charges relating to all current transactions with CERSAI on an ongoing basis.

Banks sometimes stipulate guarantees of third parties, who may be individuals or other legal entities, as additional safety. The personal guarantee of a proprietor or partners need not be stipulated because they have unlimited liability; for companies and other legal entities, whose promoters, directors or trustees have no unlimited liability towards the bank's dues, banks often stipulate personal guarantees to make the persons owning the borrower entity jointly and severally liable. The courseware gives the situations where a director's personal guarantee is useful: closely held companies (preferably of the principal members of the group holding shares rather than directors or managerial personnel functioning as such), to ensure continuity of management and a change only with the lender's knowledge (including an undertaking that there will be no change in management without the lender's consent), public limited companies other than those rated first class where the advance is unsecured, public limited companies whose financial position or cash generation is not satisfactory even though advances are secured, delays in creation of a charge, subsidiaries of parent companies whose own financial condition is not satisfactory (parent guarantee), and cases where the balance sheet shows interlocking of funds with group concerns. No consideration (commission, brokerage fees or any other form) should be paid to guarantors by the borrowing company, with an exceptional case where the new management's guarantee is essential and payment of remuneration by way of guarantee commission is allowed.
facts.locator: S01 printed pp. 484-485 (the RBI suggestions are older circulars not found in the 2025 directions read)

facts.statement: Only the owner of an asset can create a charge on it, and the procedure for creating charge over primary and collateral security is the same. The charge may be a mortgage, hypothecation, pledge, lien or assignment. As to possession of security, particularly inventory, the old favoured method was lock and key advances: goods kept in a godown with the bank holding the keys, the borrower depositing money in the cash credit account to take delivery (or a godown keeper taking and delivering goods); this has slowly changed to hypothecation, where possession remains with the borrower, and in the case of pledge the borrower may also have possession, called constructive possession, and hold the goods as an agent of the bank. Under hypothecation the possession of goods remains with the borrower; under pledge possession may remain with the borrower depending on the bank's decision.

In sole banking the bank provides working capital limits through a cash credit account of the borrower and all financial transactions should be routed through it. Drawings in the cash credit account are regulated through drawing power (DP) within the sanctioned limit. Ideally the DP is the NWC-adjusted current assets minus current liabilities (other than the cash credit outstanding) from a full statement, but such statements are available late, so banks obtain monthly statements of stocks, book debts or receivables and sundry creditors (account payable), apply margins to stocks and book debts (depending on the method of assessment) and reduce the sundry creditors to calculate the DP. Disbursal wholly by cash credit gives flexibility but makes fund management difficult for the bank and allows diversion; to stabilise utilisation a portion of the sanctioned limit is disbursed as a Loan (a fixed component) and the rest as cash credit, so that if the borrower draws little there is a debit in the loan account and a credit balance in the cash credit account.

Under the Loan System for Delivery of Bank Credit, for borrowers having an aggregate fund based working capital limit (WCL) of Rs 150 crore and above from the banking system (excluding intra-day credit facilities), the outstanding loan component (working capital loan) must be at least 60 per cent of the sanctioned fund based working capital limit, including ad hoc limits and temporary overdrafts, so drawings up to 60 per cent of the limit are allowed only from the loan component and drawings above it may be allowed as cash credit or overdraft. The bifurcation is effected after excluding export credit limits (pre-shipment and post-shipment) and the bills limit for inland sales from the working capital limit. A bank's investment in commercial paper issued by the borrower forms part of the loan component if it is sanctioned as part of the working capital limit. The minimum loan component does not apply to intra-day credit facilities, credit facilities through the Food Credit Consortium, credit facilities to Central Counterparties and credit facilities by overseas branches of the bank. The bifurcation is maintained at individual bank level in all cases, including consortium lending. The amount and tenor of the loan component are fixed by banks in consultation with borrowers, subject to the tenor being not less than seven days; the loan component may be split into working capital loans of different maturities; banks, consortia and syndicates may stipulate repayment in instalments or as a bullet, subject to the income recognition, asset classification and provisioning directions, and may roll over at the borrower's request subject to the same directions.

With effect from 1 April 2026 a framework governs the maintenance of cash credit (CC), current and overdraft (OD) accounts. A bank may provide cash credit facilities as per customers' needs without restriction under the chapter. A bank may maintain current or OD accounts without restriction for customers where the banking system's aggregate exposure (sum of all sanctioned fund based and non-fund based facilities from the banking system) is less than Rs 10 crore. Where the exposure is Rs 10 crore or more, a bank may maintain current or OD accounts only if it has a minimum 10 per cent share in the banking system's aggregate exposure or in its aggregate fund based exposure to the borrower; if no bank or only one bank meets this, the two banks with the largest exposures may maintain them; if only one bank has exposure, one more bank of the customer's choice may maintain current accounts with the first bank's no-objection certificate; if no scheduled commercial bank meets the criteria, the borrower may maintain a current account with one scheduled commercial bank of its choice on NOCs from all lending banks. A bank not meeting these criteria may maintain only collection accounts, in which funds credited must be remitted within two working days to the designated CC, current or OD account. Statutory dues and dues to the bank maintaining the collection account may be debited before remitting. Accounts under FEMA, accounts stipulated by statute or by a regulator, and accounts of regulated entities for regulated activities are exempt. A bank monitors accounts at least once every half-year; if it finds a bank ineligible it notifies the customer within one month and the account must be converted to a collection account or closed within three months; accounts are flagged in the core banking system and monitored at borrower and account level; accounts may not be used as pass-through channels for third-party transactions unless licensed; and term loans should preferably be remitted directly to the intended beneficiary's account or for the specified end use rather than routed through the borrower's account.
facts.locator: RBI_CRMD_2025 Chapter XIA paragraphs 91A-91O (inserted with effect from 1 April 2026)

facts.statement: A term loan to be disbursed in one go (for example purchase of a machine or ready house) is disbursed after the borrower deposits the margin with the bank and the loan account is debited and the entire amount remitted to the seller; where the customer has already paid the seller, satisfactory proof is taken and this is treated as part of the contribution (margin); for personal or consumption loans the amount may exceptionally be credited to the customer's account. Where project execution is spread over time, disbursement is related to progress of the project: the bank ensures that disbursal is proportionate to stages of completion and to equity infusion and other sources of finance agreed at financial closure, with the lender's independent engineer or architect certifying stages. The courseware describes three methods of bringing in promoters' equity: the promoters bring their entire contribution upfront before the bank starts disbursing; the promoters bring a certain percentage (40 to 50 per cent) upfront and the balance in stages; or the promoters agree ab initio to bring funds proportionately as the bank finances the debt portion. The last method has the greatest equity funding risk; banks should have a clear policy on the debt equity ratio (DER), ensure that the stipulated DER is maintained at all times and may adopt funding sequences so that equity funding risk is obviated.

A sole banking arrangement suits financing working capital only if the requirement is within the policy framework of the financing bank. When requirements grow beyond a bank's comfort level, several banks may form a consortium: banks formally agree to finance a borrower, choose a lead bank, which arranges periodic meetings and takes the lead in assessment, documentation, charge creation and monitoring. In multiple banking there is no formal arrangement between the banks, though they may share information on the account among themselves. Banks may evolve appropriate mechanisms for adopting a sole bank, multiple bank, consortium or syndication approach by framing ground rules. To strengthen information back-up, at the time of granting fresh facilities the bank obtains a declaration from the borrower about credit facilities already enjoyed from other lenders; in the case of existing borrowers, all banks seek a declaration from borrowers availing sanctioned limits of Rs 5 crore and above or where they know the borrower is availing facilities from other lenders, and introduce a system of exchange of information; banks exchange information about the conduct of borrowers' accounts with other lenders under consortium or multiple banking at least at quarterly intervals; the bank obtains regular certification by a professional, preferably a Company Secretary, Cost Accountant or Chartered Accountant, on compliance with statutory prescriptions; makes greater use of credit reports from Credit Information Companies; and incorporates suitable clauses in loan agreements on exchange of credit information to address confidentiality. The consortium leader or the bank with the largest exposure has the lead role in monitoring the unhedged foreign exchange exposure of entities.

Syndication of loans is normally used for sharing a long-term loan to a borrower by two or more banks, a way of sharing the risk of lending to that borrower, generally for large loans. The borrower gives a mandate to one bank (the lead bank) to arrange sanctions for the total amount on its behalf; the lead bank approaches other banks with the details, those banks appraise the proposal as per their own policies and risk appetite and take the decision; the lead bank is the liaison and common terms and conditions of sanction are agreed in a meeting of participating banks arranged by the lead bank; normally the lead bank charges a syndication fee from the borrower.

Straight Through Processing (STP) or credit underwriting engines (CUE) mean full automation of the entire cycle of the loan sanction process from application to disbursement with little to no manual interference. The process model of centralised processing began with new private sector banks in the personal segment (home, car and personal loans); centralised processing ensures uniformity in approach, sanction, documentation and post-sanction processes, and location becomes irrelevant. STP helps process more loans in minimum time with improved infrastructure, enabling customer delight and freeing human resources for complex work, and is used for MSME and other commercial lending as well. The first stepping stone is synchronisation between the maker and the user: the lender's loan policy must be captured in the software, with quantitative parameters coded as rules (ratio analysis, scores, LTV and so on). In structured lending such as personal loans it is easier to build STP: verification of KYC, ownership documents, prior charge history, credit record and score, EMI/NMI ratio and loan-to-value ratio; linkage with Unique Identification Authority of India for Aadhaar verification reduces turn-around time. The courseware notes that credit decisions depend on mitigation of all risk elements (industry, business, financial, management, default, country and exchange risks); STP must integrate third-party data and credit information company data; machine lending relies on algorithms coded on defined sets of parameters whose parameterisation should remain flexible; because STP is rule-based, omissions are almost obviated and opportunities for commission relatively less, though a wrong data feed causes a chain of bad outputs and STP must be synchronised with the core banking solution.

payload.core_explanation_md:
Before a bank releases money it must settle: **which documents** to obtain from borrower and guarantors, whether a **charge** is needed on the **primary or collateral security** and **how**, **where it must be registered**, **who holds the security**, **how the loan is disbursed** and **what RBI says**.

**Who signs:** the **borrower** and **guarantors** (so that liability can be proved in court); the borrower also signs the documents creating **charge on the primary security**; an **outside owner of collateral** must **first become a guarantor** and **then** create the charge.

payload.title: Third-party guarantees
payload.core_explanation_md:
A bank may ask for **guarantees of third parties** (individuals or other entities) as extra safety.

- **Proprietor or partners:** **no need**: they have **unlimited liability**.
- **Companies and other entities:** owners have **no unlimited liability**, so banks often take **personal guarantees** to make the owners **jointly and severally liable**.

**When a director's personal guarantee helps (courseware)**

| Situation | Why |
| --- | --- |
| **Closely held company** | Binds the **principal members of the group holding shares** (not just managerial directors) |
| **Continuity of management** | A change only with the **lender's knowledge**; **undertaking** that there will be **no change in management without the lender's consent** |
| **Public limited company not rated first class**, advance **unsecured** | Extra comfort |
| **Public limited company** with **weak finances or cash generation** though **secured** | Extra comfort |
| **Delay in creating a charge** | Covers the **interim period** |
| **Subsidiary** with weak finances | **Parent's guarantee** |
| **Interlocking of funds** with group concerns | Group risk |

**No consideration** (commission, brokerage, etc.) is to be paid to guarantors by the borrower, except exceptionally where the **new management's guarantee is essential**.
payload.expanded_explanation_md: The courseware ascribes these suggestions to RBI circulars; they are not in the 2025 directions read, so the card is held at needs_review.

self_check.prompt_text: Why is a partner's personal guarantee unnecessary for a partnership loan?
self_check.expected_takeaway: Because partners already have unlimited liability for the firm's debts.

payload.title: Types of charge and possession of security
payload.core_explanation_md:
**Only the owner of an asset can create a charge on it**; the procedure is the same for **primary** and **collateral** security. The **forms of charge**: **mortgage, hypothecation, pledge, lien, assignment**.

**Possession**

| Method | Who holds the goods |
| --- | --- |
| **Lock and key** (older favoured method) | **Bank** holds the keys of the godown; the borrower pays money into the cash credit account to take delivery |
| **Hypothecation** | The **borrower** keeps possession |
| **Pledge** | Possession **may remain with the borrower** depending on the bank's decision: **constructive possession**, the borrower holds the goods as the **bank's agent** |

What the bank holds affects the **overall risk rating** of the proposal.
payload.expanded_explanation_md: Possession matters for inventory because legal enforcement systems are still imperfect.

self_check.prompt_text: Under hypothecation, who retains possession of the goods?
self_check.expected_takeaway: The borrower.

payload.title: Disbursal of working capital: cash credit and drawing power
payload.core_explanation_md:
In **sole banking** the bank opens a **cash credit account** and **all transactions** are routed through it. Drawings are regulated by **drawing power (DP)** within the sanctioned limit.

**Ideal DP:** current assets minus other current liabilities, from a **full statement**. **Practice:** statements are late, so banks take **monthly statements** of **stocks, book debts and sundry creditors**, apply **margins** (depending on the assessment method) to **stocks and book debts** and **reduce the creditors**.

**DP = stocks (after margin) + book debts (after margin) - sundry creditors**

**Why split into loan and cash credit?** A wholly cash credit limit gives **flexibility** but makes the bank's **fund management hard** (utilisation swings with money market rates) and invites **diversion**. A fixed **loan component** plus a **cash credit** component stabilises use: if the borrower draws little, the **loan account is debited** and the **cash credit shows a credit balance**.
payload.expanded_explanation_md: The bank may require the monthly stock and book debt statement before allowing drawings above the last approved DP.

self_check.prompt_text: What is deducted from the margin-adjusted stocks and book debts to find DP?
self_check.expected_takeaway: Sundry creditors (accounts payable).

payload.title: Computing drawing power
payload.core_explanation_md: A borrower's monthly statement shows stocks of Rs 300 lakh, book debts of Rs 200 lakh and sundry creditors of Rs 80 lakh. The bank stipulates a margin of 25 per cent on stocks and 40 per cent on book debts. The sanctioned cash credit limit is Rs 280 lakh. Find the drawing power and the maximum permitted drawing.

worked_steps.description: Stocks after margin.
Book debts after margin.
DP = stocks + book debts - sundry creditors.
Drawings are limited to the lower of DP and the sanctioned limit.

payload.final_answer_with_unit: Drawing power Rs 265 lakh; maximum drawing Rs 265 lakh (below the Rs 280 lakh limit)

self_check.prompt_text: If sundry creditors were Rs 40 lakh, what would the maximum drawing be?
self_check.expected_takeaway: DP would be 225 + 120 - 40 = Rs 305 lakh, above the limit, so Rs 280 lakh.

payload.title: The loan system for large working capital borrowers
payload.core_explanation_md:
**Who:** borrowers with **aggregate fund based working capital limit of Rs 150 crore and above** from the **banking system** (intra-day facilities excluded).

**Rule:** the **loan component** (working capital loan) must be **at least 60 per cent of the sanctioned fund based limit** (including **ad hoc limits and TODs**). Drawings **up to 60 per cent** come **only from the loan component**; drawings **above it** may be **cash credit or overdraft**.

**How computed:** **exclude** **export credit limits** (pre- and post-shipment) and the **bills limit for inland sales** before bifurcating. **Commercial paper** of the borrower bought by the bank counts in the **loan component** if sanctioned as part of the limit.

**Not applicable to:** **intra-day** credit, **Food Credit Consortium**, **Central Counterparties**, **overseas branches** of the bank.

**In consortium lending** the bifurcation is kept **at individual bank level**.

**The loan itself:** amount and tenor fixed with the borrower; **tenor not less than seven days**; may be split into loans of **different maturities**; repayment in **instalments or bullet**, **rollover** on request, all **subject to the asset classification directions**.
payload.expanded_explanation_md: The point is credit discipline: large borrowers pay a fixed loan on a schedule instead of drifting in cash credit.

self_check.prompt_text: What is the minimum share of the fund based working capital limit that must be a loan for a Rs 200 crore borrower?
self_check.expected_takeaway: 60 per cent of the limit (after the exclusions), that is, the loan component.

payload.title: Splitting a large working capital limit into loan and cash credit
payload.core_explanation_md: A borrower has an aggregate fund based working capital limit of Rs 200 crore from the banking system, of which Rs 30 crore is pre- and post-shipment export credit and Rs 20 crore is a bills limit for inland sales. Find the amount on which the bifurcation is made and the minimum loan component.

worked_steps.description: Rs 200 crore is above Rs 150 crore, so the loan system applies.
Exclude export credit and the inland bills limit.
Minimum loan component is 60 per cent of the remaining limit.
The rest may be cash credit or overdraft.

payload.final_answer_with_unit: Bifurcation made on Rs 150 crore; minimum loan component Rs 90 crore; cash credit or overdraft up to Rs 60 crore

self_check.prompt_text: If the limit were Rs 120 crore, would the loan system apply?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No: the aggregate limit is below Rs 150 crore.

payload.title: Cash credit, current and overdraft accounts: the framework from 1 April 2026
payload.core_explanation_md:
| Account or customer | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| **Cash credit (CC)** | A bank may provide it per customer needs, **no restriction** |
| **Current or OD account, banking system exposure under Rs 10 crore** | **No restriction** |
| **Exposure Rs 10 crore or more** | Only a bank with **at least 10 per cent of the banking system's aggregate exposure**, **or of its fund based exposure**, may keep it |
| If **none or only one** bank meets the 10 per cent test | The **two banks with the largest exposure** may keep it |
| If **only one** bank has exposure | **One more bank of the customer's choice**, with the first bank's **NOC** |
| If **no scheduled commercial bank** meets the test | Customer may keep a current account with **one scheduled commercial bank** of choice on **NOCs from all lending banks** |
| Other banks | **Collection accounts only** |

**Collection account:** receipts must be **remitted within two working days** to the **designated** CC, current or OD account (statutory dues and the collecting bank's own dues may be debited first).

**Exempt:** accounts under **FEMA**, accounts required by **statute or a regulator**, and **regulated entities' accounts** for regulated activities.

**Monitoring:** at least **every half-year**. If a bank becomes **ineligible**, it **tells the customer within one month**, and the account is **converted to a collection account or closed within three months**. Accounts are **flagged** in the core banking system and watched **at borrower and account level**.

**No pass-through** use for **third-party** transactions (unless licensed). **Term loans** go **directly to the intended beneficiary** where identifiable rather than through the borrower's account.
payload.expanded_explanation_md: This replaces the older courseware idea that a borrower may not open an account elsewhere without the lender's permission.

self_check.prompt_text: A customer's banking system exposure is Rs 8 crore. May any bank keep a current account for them?
self_check.expected_takeaway: Yes: under Rs 10 crore there is no restriction.

payload.title: Disbursal of term loans and promoters' equity
payload.core_explanation_md:
**Single disbursal** (a machine or ready house): the borrower **deposits the margin**, the loan account is **debited** and the full amount is **remitted to the seller**. If the customer has **already paid the seller**, the bank takes **satisfactory proof** and treats it as part of the **contribution (margin)**. For **personal or consumption loans** the amount may exceptionally be **credited to the customer's account**.

**Project loans:** disbursal follows **progress**: in step with **stages of completion**, **equity infusion** and the other sources agreed at **financial closure**, with the **lender's independent engineer or architect** certifying stages.

**Three ways to bring in promoters' equity (courseware)**

| Method | Equity funding risk |
| --- | --- |
| **Entire contribution upfront** | Lowest |
| **40 to 50 per cent upfront**, balance in stages | Medium |
| **Pro rata** with the bank's disbursements (**ab initio** agreement) | **Greatest** |

Banks should have a **clear policy on the debt equity ratio (DER)**, ensure the **stipulated DER is maintained at all times** and may sequence funding so that **equity funding risk is avoided**.
payload.expanded_explanation_md: The risk is that the equity does not arrive after the bank has already lent.

self_check.prompt_text: Which equity method carries the greatest equity funding risk?
self_check.expected_takeaway: The pro rata method, where promoters bring equity as the bank finances the debt.

payload.title: Consortium and multiple banking arrangements
payload.core_explanation_md:
| | **Sole banking** | **Consortium** | **Multiple banking** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| What | One bank finances | Banks **formally agree** to finance together | Banks lend **separately** with **no formal arrangement** |
| Lead | n/a | A **lead bank** arranges meetings, **assessment, documentation, charge creation, monitoring** | None; banks may share information |

**Information rules (2025 Directions)**

1. **Fresh facilities:** obtain a **declaration** from the borrower about **credit facilities from other lenders**.
2. **Existing borrowers:** seek declarations from those with **sanctioned limits of Rs 5 crore and above**, or where the bank **knows** of other lenders; set up an **information exchange**.
3. **Exchange of conduct information** with other lenders **at least quarterly**.
4. **Regular certification** by a **professional** (preferably **Company Secretary, Cost Accountant or Chartered Accountant**) on **compliance with statutory prescriptions**.
5. Use **credit reports** from **Credit Information Companies**.
6. Put **clauses on exchange of credit information** in loan agreements (confidentiality).

**Unhedged foreign exchange exposure:** the **consortium leader** or the bank with the **largest exposure** has the **lead role** in monitoring it.
payload.expanded_explanation_md: These rules were tightened after frauds were linked to poor sharing of information among lenders.

self_check.prompt_text: At what minimum frequency do lenders exchange information on the conduct of a borrower's account?
self_check.expected_takeaway: At least quarterly.

payload.title: Syndication of loans
payload.core_explanation_md:
**Syndication** shares a **long-term loan** among **two or more banks**: a way of **spreading the risk** of a **large loan**.

1. The borrower gives a **mandate** to one bank, the **lead bank**.
2. The lead bank **approaches other banks** with the details.
3. Each bank **appraises** the proposal under **its own policy and risk appetite** and **decides**.
4. **Common terms** are agreed in a **meeting of participating banks** arranged by the lead bank.
5. The lead bank normally charges the borrower a **syndication fee**.

**Contrast with consortium:** a consortium usually shares **working capital** finance with a **formal arrangement** and a lead bank that monitors; syndication is mostly for **term loans**, arranged **loan by loan**.
payload.expanded_explanation_md: In both, the lead bank acts as the liaison.

self_check.prompt_text: What does the lead bank in a syndication usually earn from the borrower?
self_check.expected_takeaway: A syndication fee.

payload.title: Straight through processing and credit underwriting engines
payload.core_explanation_md:
**STP (credit underwriting engine):** **full automation** of the loan sanction cycle, **application to disbursement**, with **little or no manual interference**.

**Why banks use it:** **uniform** approach, sanction and documentation; **speed** with **less overhead**; **location is irrelevant**; staff freed for **complex** cases. It began with **personal segment loans** (home, car, personal) and now serves **MSME and other commercial lending**.

**How it works:** the lender's **loan policy** is coded as **rules and parameters** (ratios, scores, LTV, EMI/NMI); **data feeds** come from **KYC**, **ownership documents**, **charge history**, **credit information companies** and **Aadhaar**-linked verification.

**Risk mitigation:** a sanction is made only when **industry, business, financial, management, default, country and exchange risks** are all identified; STP integrates **third-party data**.

**Machine lending:** decisions rest on **algorithms**; parameters must stay **flexible** as conditions change.

**Omissions and commissions:** rule-based processing nearly **removes omissions** and gives **fewer chances for commissions** (biased or fraudulent judgement).

**Limits:** a **wrong data feed** produces a **chain of bad outputs**; STP must be **synchronised with the core banking solution**; it is **not a panacea**.

items.title: Documents and the credit officer's checklist
items.core_explanation_md:
Before a bank releases money it must settle: **which documents** to obtain from borrower and guarantors, whether a **charge** is needed on the **primary or collateral security** and **how**, **where it must be registered**, **who holds the security**, **how the loan is disbursed** and **what RBI says**.

**Who signs:** the **borrower** and **guarantors** (so that liability can be proved in court); the borrower also signs the documents creating **charge on the primary security**; an **outside owner of collateral** must **first become a guarantor** and **then** create the charge.

**Checklist for the credit officer**

1. **Properly stamped** (stamp duty differs by **State**).
2. **Date of execution never earlier than the date of stamping**; **date and place** stated.
3. The signers have **authority and capacity** (a partner signs **for the firm**, not personally).
4. The person signs of **free will**.
5. Documents are **filled in before** they are signed.
items.expanded_explanation_md: A blank signed document is a defective document.

self_check.expected_takeaway: No: the date of execution should never be earlier than the date of stamping.

items.title: Third-party guarantees
items.core_explanation_md:
A bank may ask for **guarantees of third parties** (individuals or other entities) as extra safety.

- **Proprietor or partners:** **no need**: they have **unlimited liability**.
- **Companies and other entities:** owners have **no unlimited liability**, so banks often take **personal guarantees** to make the owners **jointly and severally liable**.

**When a director's personal guarantee helps (courseware)**

| Situation | Why |
| --- | --- |
| **Closely held company** | Binds the **principal members of the group holding shares** (not just managerial directors) |
| **Continuity of management** | A change only with the **lender's knowledge**; **undertaking** that there will be **no change in management without the lender's consent** |
| **Public limited company not rated first class**, advance **unsecured** | Extra comfort |
| **Public limited company** with **weak finances or cash generation** though **secured** | Extra comfort |
| **Delay in creating a charge** | Covers the **interim period** |
| **Subsidiary** with weak finances | **Parent's guarantee** |
| **Interlocking of funds** with group concerns | Group risk |

**No consideration** (commission, brokerage, etc.) is to be paid to guarantors by the borrower, except exceptionally where the **new management's guarantee is essential**.
items.expanded_explanation_md: The courseware ascribes these suggestions to RBI circulars; they are not in the 2025 directions read, so the card is held at needs_review.

self_check.expected_takeaway: Because partners already have unlimited liability for the firm's debts.

items.title: Types of charge and possession of security
items.core_explanation_md:
**Only the owner of an asset can create a charge on it**; the procedure is the same for **primary** and **collateral** security. The **forms of charge**: **mortgage, hypothecation, pledge, lien, assignment**.

**Possession**

| Method | Who holds the goods |
| --- | --- |
| **Lock and key** (older favoured method) | **Bank** holds the keys of the godown; the borrower pays money into the cash credit account to take delivery |
| **Hypothecation** | The **borrower** keeps possession |
| **Pledge** | Possession **may remain with the borrower** depending on the bank's decision: **constructive possession**, the borrower holds the goods as the **bank's agent** |

What the bank holds affects the **overall risk rating** of the proposal.
items.expanded_explanation_md: Possession matters for inventory because legal enforcement systems are still imperfect.

items.title: Disbursal of working capital: cash credit and drawing power
items.core_explanation_md:
In **sole banking** the bank opens a **cash credit account** and **all transactions** are routed through it. Drawings are regulated by **drawing power (DP)** within the sanctioned limit.

**Ideal DP:** current assets minus other current liabilities, from a **full statement**. **Practice:** statements are late, so banks take **monthly statements** of **stocks, book debts and sundry creditors**, apply **margins** (depending on the assessment method) to **stocks and book debts** and **reduce the creditors**.

**DP = stocks (after margin) + book debts (after margin) - sundry creditors**

**Why split into loan and cash credit?** A wholly cash credit limit gives **flexibility** but makes the bank's **fund management hard** (utilisation swings with money market rates) and invites **diversion**. A fixed **loan component** plus a **cash credit** component stabilises use: if the borrower draws little, the **loan account is debited** and the **cash credit shows a credit balance**.
items.expanded_explanation_md: The bank may require the monthly stock and book debt statement before allowing drawings above the last approved DP.

self_check.prompt_text: What is deducted from the margin-adjusted stocks and book debts to find DP?
self_check.expected_takeaway: Sundry creditors (accounts payable).

items.title: The loan system for large working capital borrowers
items.core_explanation_md:
**Who:** borrowers with **aggregate fund based working capital limit of Rs 150 crore and above** from the **banking system** (intra-day facilities excluded).

**Rule:** the **loan component** (working capital loan) must be **at least 60 per cent of the sanctioned fund based limit** (including **ad hoc limits and TODs**). Drawings **up to 60 per cent** come **only from the loan component**; drawings **above it** may be **cash credit or overdraft**.

**How computed:** **exclude** **export credit limits** (pre- and post-shipment) and the **bills limit for inland sales** before bifurcating. **Commercial paper** of the borrower bought by the bank counts in the **loan component** if sanctioned as part of the limit.

**Not applicable to:** **intra-day** credit, **Food Credit Consortium**, **Central Counterparties**, **overseas branches** of the bank.

**In consortium lending** the bifurcation is kept **at individual bank level**.

**The loan itself:** amount and tenor fixed with the borrower; **tenor not less than seven days**; may be split into loans of **different maturities**; repayment in **instalments or bullet**, **rollover** on request, all **subject to the asset classification directions**.
items.expanded_explanation_md: The point is credit discipline: large borrowers pay a fixed loan on a schedule instead of drifting in cash credit.

self_check.expected_takeaway: 60 per cent of the limit (after the exclusions), that is, the loan component.

items.title: Cash credit, current and overdraft accounts: the framework from 1 April 2026
items.core_explanation_md:
| Account or customer | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| **Cash credit (CC)** | A bank may provide it per customer needs, **no restriction** |
| **Current or OD account, banking system exposure under Rs 10 crore** | **No restriction** |
| **Exposure Rs 10 crore or more** | Only a bank with **at least 10 per cent of the banking system's aggregate exposure**, **or of its fund based exposure**, may keep it |
| If **none or only one** bank meets the 10 per cent test | The **two banks with the largest exposure** may keep it |
| If **only one** bank has exposure | **One more bank of the customer's choice**, with the first bank's **NOC** |
| If **no scheduled commercial bank** meets the test | Customer may keep a current account with **one scheduled commercial bank** of choice on **NOCs from all lending banks** |
| Other banks | **Collection accounts only** |

**Collection account:** receipts must be **remitted within two working days** to the **designated** CC, current or OD account (statutory dues and the collecting bank's own dues may be debited first).

**Exempt:** accounts under **FEMA**, accounts required by **statute or a regulator**, and **regulated entities' accounts** for regulated activities.

**Monitoring:** at least **every half-year**. If a bank becomes **ineligible**, it **tells the customer within one month**, and the account is **converted to a collection account or closed within three months**. Accounts are **flagged** in the core banking system and watched **at borrower and account level**.

**No pass-through** use for **third-party** transactions (unless licensed). **Term loans** go **directly to the intended beneficiary** where identifiable rather than through the borrower's account.

items.title: Disbursal of term loans and promoters' equity
items.core_explanation_md:
**Single disbursal** (a machine or ready house): the borrower **deposits the margin**, the loan account is **debited** and the full amount is **remitted to the seller**. If the customer has **already paid the seller**, the bank takes **satisfactory proof** and treats it as part of the **contribution (margin)**. For **personal or consumption loans** the amount may exceptionally be **credited to the customer's account**.

**Project loans:** disbursal follows **progress**: in step with **stages of completion**, **equity infusion** and the other sources agreed at **financial closure**, with the **lender's independent engineer or architect** certifying stages.

**Three ways to bring in promoters' equity (courseware)**

| Method | Equity funding risk |
| --- | --- |
| **Entire contribution upfront** | Lowest |
| **40 to 50 per cent upfront**, balance in stages | Medium |
| **Pro rata** with the bank's disbursements (**ab initio** agreement) | **Greatest** |

Banks should have a **clear policy on the debt equity ratio (DER)**, ensure the **stipulated DER is maintained at all times** and may sequence funding so that **equity funding risk is avoided**.
items.expanded_explanation_md: The risk is that the equity does not arrive after the bank has already lent.

self_check.prompt_text: Which equity method carries the greatest equity funding risk?
self_check.expected_takeaway: The pro rata method, where promoters bring equity as the bank finances the debt.

**Information rules (2025 Directions)**

1. **Fresh facilities:** obtain a **declaration** from the borrower about **credit facilities from other lenders**.
2. **Existing borrowers:** seek declarations from those with **sanctioned limits of Rs 5 crore and above**, or where the bank **knows** of other lenders; set up an **information exchange**.
3. **Exchange of conduct information** with other lenders **at least quarterly**.
4. **Regular certification** by a **professional** (preferably **Company Secretary, Cost Accountant or Chartered Accountant**) on **compliance with statutory prescriptions**.
5. Use **credit reports** from **Credit Information Companies**.
6. Put **clauses on exchange of credit information** in loan agreements (confidentiality).

**Unhedged foreign exchange exposure:** the **consortium leader** or the bank with the **largest exposure** has the **lead role** in monitoring it.

items.title: Syndication of loans
items.core_explanation_md:
**Syndication** shares a **long-term loan** among **two or more banks**: a way of **spreading the risk** of a **large loan**.

1. The borrower gives a **mandate** to one bank, the **lead bank**.
2. The lead bank **approaches other banks** with the details.
3. Each bank **appraises** the proposal under **its own policy and risk appetite** and **decides**.
4. **Common terms** are agreed in a **meeting of participating banks** arranged by the lead bank.
5. The lead bank normally charges the borrower a **syndication fee**.

**Contrast with consortium:** a consortium usually shares **working capital** finance with a **formal arrangement** and a lead bank that monitors; syndication is mostly for **term loans**, arranged **loan by loan**.
items.expanded_explanation_md: In both, the lead bank acts as the liaison.

self_check.expected_takeaway: A syndication fee.

items.title: Straight through processing and credit underwriting engines
items.core_explanation_md:
**STP (credit underwriting engine):** **full automation** of the loan sanction cycle, **application to disbursement**, with **little or no manual interference**.

**Why banks use it:** **uniform** approach, sanction and documentation; **speed** with **less overhead**; **location is irrelevant**; staff freed for **complex** cases. It began with **personal segment loans** (home, car, personal) and now serves **MSME and other commercial lending**.

**How it works:** the lender's **loan policy** is coded as **rules and parameters** (ratios, scores, LTV, EMI/NMI); **data feeds** come from **KYC**, **ownership documents**, **charge history**, **credit information companies** and **Aadhaar**-linked verification.

**Risk mitigation:** a sanction is made only when **industry, business, financial, management, default, country and exchange risks** are all identified; STP integrates **third-party data**.

**Machine lending:** decisions rest on **algorithms**; parameters must stay **flexible** as conditions change.

**Omissions and commissions:** rule-based processing nearly **removes omissions** and gives **fewer chances for commissions** (biased or fraudulent judgement).

**Limits:** a **wrong data feed** produces a **chain of bad outputs**; STP must be **synchronised with the core banking solution**; it is **not a panacea**.
items.expanded_explanation_md: Garbage in, garbage out: the quality of the initial data decides the quality of the decision.

self_check.expected_takeaway: Error in the data fed: every later step builds on it and produces a chain of bad outputs.
